metadata.title: llm-d AI Governance Component Definition
metadata.remarks: Component definition derived from llm-d Governance Benchmark

components.title: llm-d
components.description: AI/ML component for llm-d with governance controls

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure every llm-d deployment is linked to the exact model, runtime, guide, and Kubernetes configuration

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Record the model ID and revision, llm-d guide or deployment path, Kubernetes manifests or Helm settings, accelerator profile, and runtime configuration for every governed llm-d deployment.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Completeness = governed llm-d deployments with linked model, deployment guide, Kubernetes config, and runtime metadata / total governed deployments.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure deployment-lineage completeness reaches 100% before an llm-d deployment is approved for production.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d is a Kubernetes-native distributed inference stack, so lineage must capture model, deployment recipe, and runtime shape together.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure llm-d routing, scheduler, caching, and serving topology are documented for every governed deployment

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Document the endpoint picker or routing configuration, prefill/decode topology, cache assumptions, monitoring stack, tracing scope, and hardware profile for each governed llm-d deployment.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Completeness = governed deployments with complete routing, caching, serving-topology, and hardware documentation / total governed deployments.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure serving-configuration completeness reaches 100% before deployment approval.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d behavior is shaped by distributed routing, cache awareness, and disaggregated serving configuration, so topology transparency is essential.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure served endpoint quality is benchmarked before release

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Evaluate each governed llm-d endpoint against the approved validation benchmark to confirm the served path preserves required generation quality.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Accuracy, BLEU, ROUGE, exact match, perplexity

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Run the governed evaluation suite against the llm-d endpoint and compare results to the approved baseline or champion deployment.

props.name: HF_Metric
props.value: Accuracy, BLEU, ROUGE, Exact Match, Perplexity

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure candidate serving quality metrics deviate by no more than 10% from the approved Hugging Face model-card baseline or internal champion baseline.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d is a serving stack, so quality must be validated at the endpoint level rather than assumed from offline model tests.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure token-generation latency meets the approved service objective

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Benchmark representative prompt and generation workloads against governed llm-d endpoints so latency regressions are caught before release.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Time to first token, tokens per second, p95 end-to-end latency

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Measure TTFT, decoding throughput, and end-to-end response latency over the approved benchmark workload and compute p95 values per governed endpoint.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure time to first token, tokens per second, and p95 latency remain within the approved service objective.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d positions itself around high-performance distributed inference, so latency is a first-order runtime control.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure governed llm-d deployments meet throughput targets under representative load

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Benchmark governed llm-d endpoints under representative concurrency and prompt mixes so throughput claims are validated before deployment.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Requests per second, tokens per second, concurrent-request success rate

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Run representative load tests and compute sustained throughput and successful-request ratio under the approved concurrency and hardware profile.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure throughput meets or exceeds the approved target for each governed llm-d deployment profile.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d is explicitly benchmark-oriented and designed for production throughput, so throughput validation is a direct platform control.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure KV-cache-aware routing delivers the approved latency and throughput benefit

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Validate cache-aware routing behavior so governed llm-d deployments gain the intended latency or throughput improvement without creating routing errors or hot spots.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Cache-hit rate, latency improvement, throughput improvement, routing error rate

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compare cache-aware and baseline routing under the approved workload profile, and compute cache-hit rate, performance deltas, and routing failures.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure cache-aware routing meets the approved performance target and routing error rate remains below threshold.

props.name: Threshold_Value
props.value: Project-approved routing SLO; routing error rate <1%

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d explicitly advertises KV-cache-aware routing, making it a direct serving optimization that must be validated.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure prefill/decode disaggregation is validated for the target workload and hardware profile

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Benchmark prefill/decode disaggregation so governed llm-d deployments achieve the intended efficiency without unacceptable coordination overhead or output regressions.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: TTFT, decode throughput, prefill utilization, end-to-end latency

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compare disaggregated and non-disaggregated deployments on the approved workload and hardware profile, measuring TTFT, throughput, and end-to-end latency.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure disaggregated serving meets the approved latency and throughput objective for the governed workload.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d docs and guides explicitly support prefilling/decoding disaggregation, so it needs direct validation rather than assumption.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure request routing preserves the intended serving path under distributed load

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Validate that requests are routed to the intended serving replicas or pipeline stages under governed load patterns so requests are not misdirected or starved.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Routing correctness rate, request misroute rate

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Routing correctness = governed requests handled by the intended serving path / total tested requests; misroute rate = misdirected requests / total tested requests.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure routing correctness remains above threshold and misroute rate remains below threshold for governed distributed workloads.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d adds intelligent scheduling and endpoint selection on top of serving, making routing correctness a platform-native control.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure llm-d distributed serving workflows are validated under component failure scenarios

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Test failure of prefill, decode, routing, or supporting components so governed llm-d deployments have understood recovery or degradation behavior before production use.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Failure-recovery success rate, partial-service continuity rate

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Failure-recovery success = fault-injection runs recovering within policy / total tested fault scenarios; partial-service continuity = requests served successfully under degraded mode / total tested requests during failure.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure failure-recovery success and degraded continuity remain above threshold for governed llm-d workflows.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d is a distributed serving stack, so component-failure behavior is more complex than in a single-server inference system.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure llm-d benchmark results are reproducible from approved benchmark workflows

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Use the approved llm-d benchmark workflow or equivalent reproducible benchmark setup so reported performance claims can be independently rerun and validated.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Reproducibility rate = benchmark runs that can be rerun with materially similar results / total governed benchmark reruns; repeated-run variance measured across reruns.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure benchmark reproducibility remains above threshold and repeated-run variance stays within the approved tolerance.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d emphasizes benchmarked deployment guides and has a companion benchmark workflow, so reproducibility is a core credibility control.

props.name: Sub_Risk
props.value: Missing runtime visibility across distributed components

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure governed llm-d deployments have required monitoring coverage across serving and routing components

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Enable and validate monitoring for all governed llm-d components, including endpoint picker metrics, vLLM metrics, and other required runtime signals.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Coverage = governed llm-d deployments with required component-level monitoring enabled and validated / total governed deployments.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure monitoring coverage reaches 100% before production approval.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: The llm-d docs explicitly state monitoring is enabled by default in guides and includes endpoint picker and vLLM metrics, making this a direct platform control.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure distributed tracing is enabled for governed llm-d deployments

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Enable and validate OpenTelemetry tracing across llm-d components so request flow, timing, and component interactions are visible during incident analysis.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Coverage = governed requests with sufficient distributed tracing across required llm-d components / total sampled governed requests.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure distributed traceability coverage reaches the approved threshold for all governed deployments.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: The llm-d tracing docs explicitly describe OpenTelemetry tracing across components, making this a direct observability control.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure served outputs are evaluated for PII leakage risk

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: For user-facing or sensitive models, evaluate llm-d responses for PII leakage or memorization risk before deployment and during governed monitoring.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Leakage rate = successful PII disclosures / total privacy test cases; compute precision and recall where privacy classifiers are used.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure PII leakage rate remains below threshold and privacy-detection recall remains above threshold before release.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: This is a serving-layer evaluation rule for deployed endpoints rather than a claim that llm-d itself mitigates privacy risk.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure toxicity benchmark results are measured for governed llm-d endpoints

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Evaluate governed llm-d services for toxic-generation behavior before deployment, especially for conversational or general-purpose generative endpoints.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Score benchmark outputs with a toxicity classifier and compute average toxicity plus the share of outputs exceeding the approved threshold.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure average toxicity and toxic-output rate remain below approved thresholds for release candidates.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d is specifically for LLM serving, so harmful-output regression is directly relevant at the serving layer.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure hallucination and faithfulness are benchmarked for governed endpoints

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: For generative or retrieval-augmented endpoints, run hallucination and faithfulness evaluations on the llm-d service before deployment.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Faithfulness = supported claims / total claims; hallucination rate = unsupported answers / total evaluated answers on the governed benchmark set.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure faithfulness remains above threshold and hallucination rate remains below threshold for governed release candidates.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: Applicable where llm-d is used to host LLM systems with factuality or groundedness requirements.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure factuality and unsupported-claim benchmarks are run for governed deployments

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Benchmark factuality on governed llm-d services so unsupported-claim regressions are detected before release.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Unsupported-claim rate = unsupported claims / total claims; factuality score from the approved evaluator on the benchmark suite.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure unsupported-claim rate remains below threshold and factuality remains above threshold before deployment.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: This is especially relevant where llm-d serves general-purpose or knowledge-generation endpoints.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure fairness benchmarks are evaluated for governed llm-d endpoints

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Run fairness benchmarks against the served API to ensure deployment or runtime changes do not worsen subgroup disparities.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Demographic parity difference, subgroup error rate, CrowS-Pairs or BBQ score

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compute fairness metrics on the governed benchmark set by exercising the llm-d endpoint and compare results to the approved baseline.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure subgroup disparity remains below threshold and fairness benchmark scores do not materially regress before deployment.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: Because llm-d is an inference stack, runtime changes can still affect served fairness outcomes and should be validated.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure only approved llm-d routes and services are exposed in production

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Review Kubernetes service exposure, ingress or gateway configuration, and route policies so only intended llm-d APIs and components are reachable in governed production environments.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Coverage = production llm-d deployments exposing only approved routes and services / total governed production deployments.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure approved-endpoint coverage reaches 100% before deployment approval.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d is Kubernetes-native and built around routing plus gateway integration, so endpoint exposure is a direct enterprise control.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure governed llm-d deployment artifacts pass the approved vulnerability and supply-chain review

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Validate container images, deployment artifacts, and upstream dependencies for governed llm-d deployments before production use.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Artifact-review coverage, unresolved critical vulnerability count

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Coverage = governed deployments using artifacts with completed vulnerability or supply-chain review / total governed deployments; unresolved critical vulnerability count from approved scan reports.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure artifact-review coverage reaches 100% and unresolved critical vulnerabilities remain at zero before production approval.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d is a composite distributed stack on Kubernetes, so image and dependency review is a practical deployment governance control.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure candidate promotion is backed by benchmark and readiness evidence

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Require release decisions to include evidence for quality, latency, routing correctness, monitoring readiness, tracing coverage, and deployment lineage before promoting an llm-d candidate.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Completeness = promoted candidates with complete tracked benchmark, monitoring, tracing, and lineage evidence / total promoted candidates.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure release-evidence completeness reaches 100% before candidate promotion.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: Because llm-d combines runtime behavior, routing, and distributed topology, release promotion should require both model and platform evidence.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure governed llm-d deployments cover quality, safety, privacy, routing, tracing, monitoring, and distributed-runtime readiness tests

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Build an llm-d release standard that requires representative testing across endpoint quality, latency, cache-aware routing, disaggregation, privacy, safety, fairness, monitoring, and tracing domains.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Coverage = number of mandated llm-d risk domains with active tracked evidence / total mandated risk domains in the release standard.

props.name: HF_Metric
props.value: Composite evaluation coverage based on benchmark families

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure risk-test coverage remains at or above threshold across the required llm-d validation domains.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d is a specialized distributed LLM serving stack, so release readiness must cover both model behavior and distributed-runtime evidence.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure served models have complete model-card-style documentation

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Attach intended use, limitations, benchmark results, fairness results, privacy assumptions, and deployment constraints to each governed model served through llm-d.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Completeness = completed required transparency fields / total required transparency fields for each governed served model.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure model transparency completeness reaches 100% before production approval.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: Even though llm-d is a serving stack, model-card-style transparency remains necessary for governed deployments.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure deployment topology, hardware assumptions, and observability scope are documented for governed llm-d systems

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Document routing components, scheduler behavior, disaggregation topology, hardware profile, monitoring stack, and tracing scope for each governed llm-d system.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Completeness = completed required architecture and deployment fields / total required fields in the approved transparency checklist.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure system transparency completeness reaches 100% before production approval.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: llm-d systems are defined by distributed serving topology and hardware assumptions as much as by the model itself, so architecture transparency is essential.
